text:
alexm: Pasting quick summary of an nsys run — noticing repeated host->device memcpy spikes immediately before tiny kernels. Hostcopy seems to be serialized and kernels are starved, overall tail latency up ~18% on small-batch inference.

maria_s: Can you drop the nsys command and a short screenshot of the timeline crop?

alexm: Ran with: ```nsys profile --output nsys_kv_evict --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --sample=none --force-overwrite ./bin/serve --profile-run --model gpt-small --batch-size 2``` Timeline: cpu thread submits prefetch -> 3x H2D memcpy on copy engine -> tiny kernel (1-2ms) -> gap ~6-12ms -> next batch. Copy engine activity overlaps other streams but kernels don't overlap each other.

alexm: Observed pattern across 5 traces: memcpy initiates late (CPU wake jitter), and sometimes memcpy itself waits on page-in (VM activity). NVTX shows kvcache evict events right before the big memcpys.

tj: Could be CPU scheduling preemption delaying the enqueue of memcpy ops. Perf shows big involuntary context-switches on the thread that drives copy submission?

rohan: Agree. Another hypothesis: our kvcache eviction path calls madvise/munmap then immediate cudaMemcpy which hits kernel path that page-faults into userspace -> hostcopy stalls. If eviction triggers right before prefetch we reintroduce full H2D instead of cheap KV lookup.

maria_s: Do we have perfetto flamegraph showing page-faults or futex waits on the submitter thread?

alexm: Quick perf record I ran: ```perf record -g -F 99 -p <pid> -- sleep 10``` then ```perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded && flamegraph.pl out.folded > perf.svg``` Shows spikes in do_page_fault and swapin, and a bunch of schedule() wakes.

tj: If the CPU thread is preempted between preparing the CUDA memcpy and calling cuLaunchKernel, the copy can get queued late and end up serialized behind prior memcpys. On top of that, copy engine may be contended by other clients. Check copy engine queue depth.

alexm: I inspected nsight timeline: copy engine (DMA) shows bursts ~50ms apart with long tails; kernels are microscale and sit idle waiting for K/V prefetch results. Also noticed occasional stream stall markers where OSrt shows "stall: waiting for host".

rohan: Two quick experiments to triage: 1) pin the prefetch/submit thread to an isolated core (taskset) to remove preemption, 2) increase kvcache size to avoid eviction and see if memcpy events disappear.

maria_s: Also try enabling CUDA mem pooling (CUDA_MEMPOOL_REUSE_WAIT) or set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES env for better stream locality? Could also try disabling unified memory paging.

alexm: Will try 1 & 2. Also swapping batching heuristic: switch from aggressive microbatching (flush on token boundary) to 25ms fixed window to see if coalescing reduces small-kernel sandwich.

tj: For nsight captures, add OS trace flags: `--trace=osrt,nvtx,cuda,ipc` and use `nsys stats` to export copy engine timeline CSV. That CSV can show gaps between memcpy submit and start.

alexm: Ran taskset + no-evict: latency tail dropped ~12%, number of H2D memcpys per second dropped by ~60%. Preliminary win.

rohan: Nice. If that holds, next step is to make the submit thread SCHED_FIFO with low overhead or move prefetch responsibilities to a dedicated thread pinned to an isolated core. Also consider marking kvcache buffers with MADV_DONTDUMP / MADV_POPULATE to avoid page faults on first access.

maria_s: Did you capture a final nsys after the change? We should keep before/after traces for postmortem.

alexm: I captured a follow-up: `nsys_kv_evict_fixed.nsys-rep`. Will upload to the trace bucket. Differences: memcpy bursts are gone, copy engine utilization more uniform, kernels overlap better.

infra-bot: Upload complete: s3://redwood-traces/nsys/2425006789/nsys_kv_evict_fixed.nsys-rep :thumbsup:

tj: Great. Action items: (1) add thread pinning to kvcache prefetch path as short-term fix, (2) add telemetry to count evictions per inference request and emit nvtx spans when eviction happens, (3) prototype scheduling the prefetch thread SCHED_FIFO in a perf-isolated box.

rohan: Also add guarded madvise/populate on kvcache insert path behind a flag so we can A/B test memory-touch cost vs pagefault cost.

alexm: I'll open a PR with thread affinity + flag + a short doc on how to reproduce the nsight workflow and include the perf/nsys commands and the specific regions to crop.

maria_s: Thanks — please cc me on the PR. :eyes:
